context: The integer n is positive. The left column, “Descend,” lists calls. The right column, “Unwind,” gives their return expressions. Ellipses stand for intermediate calls. The table shows the first and last levels in the figure. For small n, only the necessary levels occur.

frames.explanation: The call recur(n) calls recur(n−1). The argument decreases by 1 at each level until recur(1). This row is labeled “Reach the base case,” with a rightward arrow marking the start of the returns. First, recur(1) returns 1. Then recur(2) receives 1 and computes 2 + 1 = 3. Next, recur(3) receives 3 and computes 3 + 3 = 6. In general, recur(k) must wait for its child call to return before it can add k. The additions therefore take place as the calls unwind.
frames.title: Summing with ordinary recursion

result: Once the terms have been added on the way back up, the original call recur(n) returns 1 + 2 + … + n.
summary: Reduce the sum to its base case, then add one term at each level as the calls return.
